title: Clean and Unclean Animals
intro: God gave Israel detailed rules about which animals they could eat. These rules set Israel apart from other nations and taught them to distinguish between clean and unclean in all areas of life.

items.title: Land Animals - Clean
items.text: Animals that both have a divided hoof AND chew the cud. Examples: cow, sheep, goat, deer, gazelle, roe deer.

items.title: Land Animals - Unclean
items.text: Animals that lack one or both of these traits. Camel (chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof), pig (has a divided hoof but does not chew the cud), hare, rock badger.

items.title: Water Animals - Clean
items.text: Everything in the water that has fins AND scales may be eaten.

items.title: Water Animals - Unclean
items.text: All without fins and scales are detestable: shellfish, eel, squid, etc.

items.title: Birds - Unclean
items.text: Birds of prey and scavengers: eagle, vulture, sea eagle, kite, falcon, raven, ostrich, owl, gull, hawk, great horned owl, cormorant, ibis, bat.

items.title: Insects
items.text: Winged creeping things are unclean. Exception: Locusts with jumping legs (locust, solam, hargol, hagab) are clean.

items.title: Creeping Things
items.text: All creeping things on the ground are unclean: mole, mouse, lizards, gecko, chameleon.

footer.title: Meaning Today
footer.content: In the New Testament, Jesus abolished the food laws (Mark 7:19) and showed Peter that all animals are clean (Acts 10). The rules taught Israel holiness - to be set apart for God. For Christians today, it is about being set apart morally, not in dietary choices.
